datasets.title: British Indian Ocean Territory: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/iot-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values from VIIRS satellite observations are collected at 10-day intervals. Anomalies are calculated at each grid cell by computing the deviation of FAPAR from a long-term mean baseline spanning 2012 to the most recent complete year, enabling detection and monitoring of agricultural drought impacts on vegetation productivity.

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Provides FAPAR satellite observations from the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) used to calculate vegetation anomalies relative to long-term baseline (2012-present)

sources.name: Copernicus
sources.description: Copernicus Earth observation program providing the FAPAR biophysical parameter data and anomaly calculations for drought monitoring
